reviews.text:
The doctor's overwhelming lack of experience was striking, and the nurses seemed listless as they emerged from the back door.

They only talked about databases, never discussing actual treatment cases or explaining treatment plans. Furthermore, even though it was a daytime visit and not an emergency night, the consultation fee was quite high.

No treatment or procedures were performed, and no medication was prescribed.

While this might be understandable for a cold or minor illness, I felt strongly indignant at such treatment given the suspected serious illness.

My honest opinion is that I absolutely would not recommend this hospital to anyone who considers their dog or cat a cherished family member.

I took my pet in for a check-up.

Due to an emergency, my pick-up time was delayed by about two hours from the original schedule.

While I understand that this is unavoidable, it would be helpful if parking fees were reimbursed in such cases.

I visited the hospital for emergency treatment of my dog ​​at night.
I was relieved to find it a clean and well-equipped hospital.
The nurses also responded quickly.

I used their services for a nighttime rabbit checkup for the first time in several years.
Honestly, I think it depends on the skill of the veterinarian on duty at the time.
The service was generally good.
The veterinarian this time was excellent.
The fee is quite high, but it's unavoidable for a nighttime emergency consultation.

I went to the emergency room at night.

They treated me immediately, and kindly and thoroughly explained an illness that my usual clinic hadn't been able to detect. They admitted me to the hospital.

There's no parking lot, so I parked in a nearby coin-operated parking lot, but it's cheap at night, which is great.

I'm incredibly grateful to the doctors.

I believe they offer high-quality services and you can entrust your child to them with confidence.
They provide thorough explanations and reports as needed.
They seem to be part of the Aeon group, and the staff are very pleasant.
I would especially recommend them in cases of serious illness.

I felt uneasy about the handling of eye drops and the way inquiries were handled.

During the examination, the doctor explained that I should use Betratan in the right eye and Azorga in the left eye, but the medication bag I received at the reception desk had the left and right sides reversed. Even after pointing this out, I received no clear explanation or guidance on preventing recurrence.

Furthermore, when I inquired about my dog's head tilting to the left while continuing to use the eye drops, I was told that the doctor was unavailable and that they would call me back, but I received no call that day or the next.

While the causal relationship with the symptoms is unclear, I felt the response was insufficient given the potential safety implications. I hope for a review of the system.

The doctor's explanation itself was thorough, but I felt uneasy about the overall response.

I would advise against using this clinic if there are other emergency clinics available, as they are not skilled at handling animals, and neither the veterinarian nor the nurses showed any affection towards them.

My cat had diarrhea, so I took her in late at night. A female veterinarian was in charge, but she remained expressionless throughout and seemed completely uninterested in the animal she was examining. I was already worried at this point, but I became even more anxious after she explained the procedure and I left my cat in the examination room for testing.

Owners are not allowed to be present during examinations, which is the hospital's rule, but while waiting for the procedure, I could hear screams and thrashing sounds I'd never heard before. I understand that my cat may have been causing trouble by struggling, but the noises and conversations I heard clearly suggested that they weren't handling the animal with care.

After a while, I was called into the examination room and told that "the examination cannot be done without anesthesia because the cat is struggling." Since my cat is elderly, I wanted to avoid general anesthesia if possible, but I had no choice but to have the examination done under anesthesia. In the end, after listening to the female doctor's hesitant explanation of the blood test results, I left the hospital feeling even more anxious than before the examination.

My dog ​​is naturally timid and dislikes strangers and hospitals, and I kept telling myself that the doctors' response was unavoidable because it was a late-night emergency. However, after seeing how my regular vet and other emergency hospitals handled things, I realized that it wasn't that simple.

There are hospitals that can skillfully draw blood and take X-rays using Elizabethan collars or towels without anesthesia, and even in emergencies where the cause isn't clear or treatment options are limited, there are many hospitals that provide compassionate care and support to both the owner and the pet.

Unless it's an unavoidable situation where this is the only hospital that will treat your pet, I would recommend using a different hospital.

Thank you for your continued support.

Last time, you accepted my appointment even though it was right at closing time, which was a great help. This is a hospital I can trust.

I was in the care of my cat for three days during her hospital stay. When I went to visit her, she was relaxing with her belly exposed even while receiving an IV drip, so I think she was very comfortable there (lol). The explanations were clear and I felt at ease leaving her in their care. I felt that they not only cared about the animals but also respected the owner's wishes.

My regular vet's doctor was hospitalized during an examination, so I was referred here. Dr. Yamaguchi, who was my first visitor, treated me with sincerity and genuine care, even though it was my first time. I wondered if he was the head doctor! He then connected me with Dr. Sasaki, a Type 1 oncologist (only 49 in Japan). Dr. Sasaki's examination was incredibly thorough and gentle, and I have no doubts about the results. Even for my 14-year-old senior Pekingese, they didn't give up and presented many options.

The doctor who explained the medication was also very thorough! I was so happy that they praised my precious dog!

The reception staff were also kind. They were very helpful when I called beforehand to ask about parking!

The only reason for the four stars is that the examination room isn't very spacious, so all tests, including ultrasounds, had to be left with them. This is unavoidable, and it's the same at other hospitals, but my regular vet is a rare hospital where you can actually see the ultrasound during the examination.

Aside from the examination room, it's a five-star hospital!!

It took almost an hour by car, but I'm so glad I was able to get an appointment!

They also offer evening appointments, so they're a great help to the Joto area!

Too inefficient
Long waiting time
The worst

Supplement Recommendation Shop
If your pet has any abnormalities, they'll recommend supplements right away!
Consultations? Treatment? Medication? Rather than all that, they'll recommend supplements!
Supplements first! They don't offer treatments, but they do have plenty of supplements!

I've used their services several times, and they're incredibly kind and attentive during both their after-hours and regular daytime appointments.

I sometimes wonder if I should switch my primary care physician.

The phone service was pleasant, which made me feel at ease when I came to the hospital.

The explanations were kind and thorough, making this a very trustworthy hospital.

Since it was an emergency, the fee was accordingly high, but I appreciated that they discussed the cost and procedures beforehand.

I think their service was quick and accurate.

The doctor was very good, but I hope that I'll never need to take my pet there again.

My cat received treatment from Dr. Kenji Muroi.

Dr. Muroi began the examination with a basic check of the heart and lung sounds, and was able to identify and treat the cause of my cat's ailments, which are often difficult to detect.

Since then, my cat has been healthy and has not had any recurrences.

Honestly, there is a waiting time even with an appointment, but I'm willing to wait if it means being seen by Dr. Muroi.

I've taken my dog ​​to this clinic several times for vaccinations, and they are incredibly kind and gentle with pets, making sure my dog ​​doesn't develop a fear of the vet!

They're also very skilled at administering injections, so I felt completely at ease leaving my dog ​​in their care!

The daytime Petemo Animal Hospital and the nighttime Tokyo Higashi clinic are located in the same place.

Although there is a nighttime fee, it is extremely helpful that they accept patients at any time.

Because the nighttime and daytime hospitals are seamlessly integrated, pets can be admitted at night and then seen by the daytime veterinarian, providing 24-hour peace of mind.

I know it must be very hard work for the veterinarians and nurses, but I sincerely hope they continue this system.
I took my dog ​​in late at night because he had swallowed a foreign object, but everything went smoothly, and they even gave him an IV drip.

My pet's condition suddenly worsened overnight, and I had to give it emergency treatment. Unfortunately, it never recovered, but because I had informed them of its condition by phone, they were able to carry out tests and treatment immediately upon arrival. All the staff, including the veterinarian, animal nurse, and receptionist, were polite and always considerate of the pet owner's feelings. There was also a sense of security that the facility was open 24 hours a day, and sick pets came in at any time.

The administrative staff, such as the receptionists, seemed careless.

- The patient card I received on my first visit belonged to someone else.

- I was advised to have a thorough examination at another hospital, and an appointment was made for me later through a referral. However, when I received a phone call, I was given a completely different date. It was totally different from the date and time I had requested, and even when I asked for clarification, they insisted that's what they had been told. (Later, I received a call from the doctor informing me that an appointment had been made for the requested date.)

While I wouldn't mind these kinds of things at a human hospital, at a veterinary hospital, you have no choice but to trust the hospital, so this carelessness bothers me.

I will not be going back.

Our 17-year-old dog suffered a status epilepticus, and we sought emergency care at this hospital for the first time.

Thanks to the doctors' dedicated treatment, there were signs of temporary recovery, but sadly, she crossed the Rainbow Bridge 🌈. We wanted her to be with us at home during her final moments, so we went to pick her up, and she passed away in the taxi on the way home.

Although it wasn't at home, she passed away so peacefully and calmly on my husband's lap. We are filled with gratitude to the doctors, nurses, and staff at the hospital for their understanding and support during this difficult time.

If we ever have another dog in our lives, we would like to seek care at this hospital again. Thank you so much.

It was the middle of the night on a Saturday, so my usual hospital was closed, and they referred me here.

They said so many reassuring things to ease my worries, which made me feel much better.

My senior dog, who turned 16 in March, has many chronic illnesses and I've had to take him to the vet several times in the middle of the night. It was always the head veterinarian who treated him. His explanations were thorough, and I felt confident taking him to this hospital again.

However, this time it was a new doctor, and I was a little anxious. I left him there, planning to pick him up in the evening after an overnight stay. That was a mistake.

About two hours before I was supposed to pick him up, I received a call saying he had gone into cardiac arrest. They performed CPR, but his heart never started again, and he had passed away.

I tried to control my panic and drove to pick him up.

My dog ​​has diabetes, kidney failure, liver cancer, and many other chronic illnesses, so I was prepared for the worst.

However, when I asked about the cause of death, I was told it wasn't related to his chronic illnesses; he had a growth in his throat that had caused him to suffocate.

My mind went blank, wondering why it happened so suddenly. The female doctor explained things matter-of-factly, and when I asked "why," she only said they didn't know the exact cause. Filled with sadness and anger, I went to my regular vet the next day and told them what happened. They said the head veterinarian should have explained it properly, and that the cause of death was strange.

I called the hospital again and spoke to a different male doctor. He explained things in more detail than the day before, but ultimately it was the same thing. No matter what I said, my child wouldn't come back, and I decided I couldn't go on any further and hung up.
The image of his face as he said goodbye, "See you tomorrow," still haunts me, and the tears won't stop.
I wish I had brought him home then.
Even a good hospital can turn into hatred depending on the doctor.
Even though the cause of death is unknown, I was still charged exorbitant medical and hospitalization fees.

To Dr. Akema
From December 31st of last year to March 19th of this year,
we were repeatedly admitted to and discharged from the hospital,
and I'm so sorry for always making unreasonable requests and causing you so much trouble.
I believe that Carl 🐶 survived because of your support.
It's a great loss and sadness for the Akiyama family that you're going to another clinic, but if there's another opportunity, please examine Carl and Leo again.
Thank you very much. 🙇‍♂️

My youngest daughter (🐱), who is usually very energetic, had no appetite, so I called for a consultation.
Just to be safe, I called for an emergency night visit. Because I had contacted them in advance, they started checking for any abnormalities with palpation and a stethoscope before I even finished filling out the questionnaire. After I finished filling it out, they asked me more questions and explained everything carefully. It's very reassuring to know they provide nighttime care. Thank you very much!

I went to the emergency room for the past two days,
and he was admitted yesterday. Despite going to the emergency room, the difference in attitude was striking. What if this were a human?

Wouldn't his hands move before his mouth?

Before the morning handover, the hospital director told me:
"He's stable, for better or worse," so I went to visit him in the evening since the attending physician was scheduled for the night.

During the visit, while receiving an explanation from Dr. M, who had taken over, I was the one who discovered something was wrong with my child, even though the attending physician was right there.

Even in a critical situation, the first thing they did was explain.

He said, "I'll get the stethoscope first."

Was that unnecessary delay in speaking?

The moment he got on the examination table:
"If he goes into cardiac arrest, should we intubate him?" While he was suffering.

At the time of the visit, I was told they had administered an injection to raise his blood sugar due to low blood pressure, and that they removed the IV because it had risen too much.

If this condition hadn't changed, how much more critical would it have become? From his admission in the morning until evening (7:30 PM), there was absolutely no contact.

The readings remained three times normal for 10 hours.
In the end, they even got the age wrong, saying, "He survived."

Shouldn't they have responded by brushing me off before I could even speak?

Furthermore, even after getting him on the examination table, they couldn't properly attach the electrocardiogram and just fumbled around with it.

I was complaining to the doctor while my child was in critical condition.

Nothing was done.

If there was a reason why nothing was done, a proper doctor would explain.

What were the four people, including young assistant Dr. M, doing just standing around the examination table?

I still wish that the last words the child heard were requests to you all, and the words, "We're going home! Let's go home quickly! We're going home now!"

When I asked you, who were just silently watching, "Is it really stopped? Aren't you going to check the pupils?!"

You replied, "There's no heartbeat, so should we check?"

Were you just waiting for death?

The test results differed from the previous day's, and there was absolutely no mention of a critical period, especially tonight.

There was no communication whatsoever from Dr. M, who took over during the day, regarding any changes in her condition.

If it had only been an IV drip, I would have gone there preparing to discharge her. I arrived 30 minutes ago, went inside, saw her face, and stayed until the end—only about 40 minutes.

Less than 10 minutes after seeing her face, her condition changed, and I kept them waiting.

I think she endured and waited patiently.

They only gave manual-based explanations, but there are no manuals for medical procedures!!

At the very least, it wasn't a situation where she would die in half a day.

I went to the hospital based on my own judgment, but if I had been another hour later, I wouldn't have made it. It's absolutely terrible.

Their experience and knowledge are far too low.

I don't like their actions, which are based on the assumption that she doesn't have long to live!

I truly feel terrible about what happened...
I'm still grieving.

How much care and attention did they really give her during that short half-day hospital stay?

They were laying him flat even though he looked like he was in pain.
It was an emergency hospital, so I didn't know anything about it, but I believed the other staff were the same because the director handled him so carefully. I never imagined they wouldn't even contact me about his sudden change in condition.
Of course, I confirmed this with the director when I went home.
I mean, wouldn't they normally contact you?

I could hear laughter and chatter coming from outside the ICU where the emergency animals were (right behind the reception). Why were they acting so busy when they had that much time?

They were definitely looking after the animals!

I just wanted to see his face as soon as I arrived.

I wrote a post about it.

I'm speechless.

*Later*
Even when I took him home that day, there was no explanation whatsoever. So, I requested a visit, and my family and I went back a week later.

We met with Dr. M and the director.

The hospital director tried to protect his subordinates, saying that coordination hadn't gone well, but when you're in charge of a hospitalized child, coordination is the least of your worries, isn't it?

Dr. M, who took over, was inexplicably sulky and answered questions with mockery.

All of his answers were just, "That was the intention."

There are good things in other reviews, but true character is revealed in critical situations.

This is what actually happened to my child.

I hope your pet experiences the same pain.

I will never forgive you for treating my precious child so poorly.

It's almost been two years, but I haven't forgotten. I will never forgive you.

If you're going to this emergency hospital,
if you don't have deep medical knowledge, and especially if you can't make calm judgments in a critical situation, you shouldn't go.

Even if you know what to do, it won't come to mind in the moment, and you'll suffer from regret like me.

You will definitely pay the price for treating pets so poorly.

Our elderly dog ​​underwent surgery at this clinic.

We are truly grateful for the careful explanations, meticulous surgery, and attentive post-operative care provided by the doctors, who considered each dog's personality and physical condition.

It's incredibly helpful to have a second opinion available, even when our regular vet is closed, so we can seek treatment without worry.

I read the reviews before our initial visit, and I think the waiting time is reasonable considering the doctors and staff's sincere dedication to helping each and every dog.

As I myself am a patient at a national university hospital, I didn't feel like I waited very long for payment or billing.

In fact, sometimes it takes over an hour to complete the billing process when visiting two departments in the morning and afternoon.

I understand the feelings of those who are worried about their dogs, but I hope that each and every pet owner in the waiting room will think of their own dog and return home healthy.

I went to get heartworm medication after a camping trip, and despite explaining the situation,

First, they made my dog ​​get tested for heartworm (it was negative). Then, they prescribed heartworm medication that also contained flea and tick medication.

What's the reason for checking for heartworm infection?

I could understand if they wouldn't prescribe medication if the dog wasn't infected.

If they prescribe it regardless of infection status, then the test is pointless.

I've had similar cases in the past.

I think they just want to get that 10,000 yen fee for a single consultation.

These kinds of places do a lot of unnecessary tests and, in some cases, unnecessary treatments, so I switched to a different hospital.

I'm really glad I did.

*This happened several years ago. I hope things have improved since then.
It seems they offer after-hours consultations, so that's helpful!

Very thorough.
The explanations are logical and easy to understand.
